The ETF remains above its 200-day moving average, confirming a healthy long-term uptrend. While the Fear & Greed index shows mild fear at 38, this is not a signal to pause — it simply means sentiment hasn't turned euphoric, which is actually a reasonable environment for steady accumulation.
history.this_month: Contribute your normal monthly DCA amount — no need to increase or decrease. Prices are near all-time highs, but for a long-term accumulator that is not a reason to pause; time in the market consistently beats timing the market. history.long_term_thesis: VOO provides low-cost, diversified exposure to 500 of the largest U.S. companies, capturing the long-run compounding power of the American economy. With a massive $1.6 trillion AUM base and Vanguard's structural cost efficiency, this ETF is one of the strongest long-term wealth-building vehicles available to retail investors.
history.risks: The primary risk is valuation — U.S. large-cap equities are trading at elevated P/E multiples historically, meaning forward returns over the next 5–10 years may be more modest than the past decade. Concentration in the top 10 holdings (heavily tech) also means a sector-specific downturn could weigh disproportionately on the index. These are long-term considerations, not reasons to stop accumulating, but worth balancing with international or small-cap exposure over time.
history.add_rationale: Already held and should remain the core anchor of any long-term U.S. equity portfolio. Continue regular monthly contributions and resist the urge to pause simply because prices are near highs — dollar-cost averaging is designed precisely to remove that emotional friction.
